newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Maskhadov brings former rival into Chechen cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Maskhadov brings former rival into Chechen cabinet.

text.p: Chechnya's new leader Aslan Maskhadov has appointed a former rival for the presidency, Movladi Udugov, as the breakaway region's foreign minister, Interfax news agency said on Sunday.

Maskhadov, who was inaugurated as Chechnya's first post-war president last Wednesday, also named Musa Doshukayev as first deputy prime minister, a post he held under the late rebel leader Dzhokar Dudayev, Interfax said.

Udugov served as information minister during the Chechen separatists' 21-month bloody fight against Russian troops and often defeated Moscow's propaganda machine, broadcasting messages by satellite phone from mountain hideouts.

Both Maskhadov and Udugov are staunch supporters of Chechen independence, which they regard as a fait accompli after their military victory despite Moscow's continued insistence that the tiny mountainous region remain inside the Russian Federation.

Maskhadov plans to combine the posts of president and prime minister, taking full responsibility for the new government which must oversee the start of economic reconstruction in a land still heavily scarred by war, Russian agencies said.
The softly-spoken former Soviet artillery colonel is also expected to take over the defence portfolio.

On Saturday Chechens took part in a second round of voting for parliamentary elections but preliminary results released on Sunday showed the average turnout was not more than 30 percent, Interfax said.
Under the Chechen constitution, this means the poll is invalid and a new round of voting must be held in two months' time, it said.
Polling took place on Saturday in nearly 60 Chechen districts where no candidate had won a clear majority in the first round on January 27.
